claims.text: Tungsten-based high-entropy alloys are relevant candidate structural materials for fusion plasma-facing components.
Controlled heat treatments can systematically vary the coherence and spatial distribution of in-situ nanoprecipitates in the proposed tungsten-based HEA.
Nanoprecipitate coherence and spacing govern high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten-based HEAs.
Coherent nanoprecipitates with controlled spacing lower barriers to dislocation transmission.
Coherent, appropriately spaced nanoprecipitates diffuse or mitigate localized stress concentrations at precipitate-matrix interfaces.
Greater dislocation mobility can enhance crack-tip blunting or shielding and thereby resist crack propagation.
Precipitate characteristics can affect plastic strain in a refractory HEA.
The relevant high-temperature regime approaches 0.5–0.6 of the melting temperature.
Above approximately 0.5–0.6 Tm, diffusion-controlled deformation can activate and soften refractory alloys.
Using minimal irradiation isolates thermal effects in the proposed comparison.
Optimally tuned nanoprecipitate coherence and spacing will produce greater plastic strain capacity than the unmodified baseline alloy.
Optimally tuned nanoprecipitate coherence and spacing will produce greater fracture toughness than the unmodified baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies under fusion-relevant high-temperature conditions.
The effectiveness of the proposed mechanism may diminish under severe irradiation.
The effectiveness of the proposed mechanism may diminish at extreme strain rates.
The relative contributions of nanoprecipitate coherence, spacing, and interactions with other defects have not been quantitatively determined.
Heat-treated samples with differing precipitate coherence and spacing will be compared with an unperturbed baseline using high-temperature tensile, fracture, and TEM measurements.
The mechanism is falsified if precipitate changes produce neither systematic mechanical-property differences nor correlations with dislocation or crack behavior.
